fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH CUTS. One adversarial validator read arXiv 2611.27017 (abstract and full HTML, Table II, limitations, future work, acknowledgments) and the Nalaquq site. Conditions: (1) a preprint posted November 20th, 2026, not peer reviewed; (2) never used in a real search, the scenario was simulated, real human-in-the-loop integration is future work, nobody was found or rescued; (3) researchers arranged the items, mostly donated by the community, the paper calls them QSAR-selected search indicators, say nothing more about the community's role; (4) each number stays with its scene and its own threshold, mudflat about 56% precision and 55% recall, swamp grass about 99% precision and 29% recall, never one setting; low recall explained only in the paper's words (filtering can suppress true detections, higher thresholds can suppress camouflaged objects); (5) never claim the reason for onboard processing is missing internet, the paper says it removes dependence on data offloading; (6) never call SABL unsupervised; (7) SABL augments existing search methods, two scenes of subarctic tundra only; (8) affiliations as printed; (9) Quinhagak described only with sourced facts, never speak for residents or QSAR members, no quotes from the community.

claims.spoken: This comes from a preprint posted to arXiv on November 20th. It hasn't been peer reviewed yet.
claims.verbatim_source: "[Submitted on 20 Nov 2026]
requires: a preprint, not peer reviewed

claims.spoken: The authors call their system SABL, short for Spectral Anomaly Based Localization.
claims.verbatim_source: "We present SABL, an edge-computing pipeline for on-drone Spectral Anomaly-Based Localization.
requires: a preprint, not peer reviewed

claims.spoken: The authors are from Binghamton University, Hampden Sydney College and Nalaquq, a company based in Quinhagak.
claims.verbatim_source: "Nalaquq, LLC, Quinhagak, AK 99655 USA
requires: Gyabaah Kyere is Hampden-Sydney only, Sean Gleason is listed at both
write Nalaquq, LLC exactly

claims.spoken: Search crews usually fly aircraft with regular cameras and infrared cameras.
claims.verbatim_source: "WSAR teams commonly use crewed and uncrewed aircraft to collect conventional visible (EO/RGB) and infrared (IR) imagery
requires: say infrared as the paper does, add no outside thermal claims

claims.spoken: Those cameras can miss people who are camouflaged, wearing insulated clothing, or not giving off a usual heat signature.
claims.verbatim_source: "deliberately camouflaged, insulated, or lacking a conventional thermal signature
requires: the paper's motivation, not a measured result

claims.spoken: Hyperspectral cameras can pick up differences in what things are made of that ordinary images don't show.
claims.verbatim_source: "These measurements can expose material-composition differences that are not apparent in conventional imagery
requires: no claim that it sees through objects

claims.spoken: The catch is that they produce so much data that processing it on the drone in real time is hard.
claims.verbatim_source: "but its high data volume challenges real-time on-drone processing

claims.spoken: Processing on the drone means the data doesn't have to be offloaded first.
claims.verbatim_source: "Onboard processing removes dependence on data offloading, thereby allowing potential indicators
requires: never say the reason was a lack of internet or cell service

claims.spoken: The camera records 150 bands of light between 400 and 1000 nanometers.
claims.verbatim_source: "captures 150 bands in VNIR (400-1000 nm)

claims.spoken: It scans like a push broom, capturing the ground one line at a time.
claims.on_screen: PUSH-BROOM · ONE LINE AT A TIME
claims.verbatim_source: "many UAS-compatible systems use push-broom sensors that acquire imagery one line at a time

claims.spoken: The computer doing all the work was a Raspberry Pi 4B.
claims.verbatim_source: "We executed this system on a Raspberry Pi 4B connected to the camera via a Cat6 Ethernet cable

claims.spoken: It scores every line with a Reed Xiaoli anomaly detector, then groups the flagged pixels using a method called DBSCAN.
claims.verbatim_source: "exponentially moving Reed-Xiaoli (ERX) anomaly detection and DBSCAN spatial filtering
requires: never call it unsupervised

claims.spoken: For each cluster, it reports a GPS position searchers can go and check.
claims.verbatim_source: "SABL also reports the GPS position of the center-most point in the cluster

claims.spoken: It handles each scanline in about 5.7 milliseconds, faster than the camera's 10 millisecond interval.
claims.verbatim_source: "It processes hyperspectral scanlines at 5.67-5.73 ms per line, meeting the camera's 10-ms acquisition interval
requires: a preprint, not peer reviewed

claims.spoken: Without the full pipeline, the detector alone took about 21 milliseconds per line on the Pi, too slow for real time.
claims.verbatim_source: "On the embedded device, ERX achieves average line processing times of 21.34 ms
requires: optional detail

claims.spoken: The data comes from a 10 day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue in Alaska.
claims.verbatim_source: "10-day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue (QSAR)
requires: name the organization exactly
data collection, not a real search

claims.spoken: Quinhagak Search and Rescue is a nonprofit that trains and organizes volunteer responders.
claims.verbatim_source: "Quinhagak Search and Rescue (QSAR), is a non-profit organization which trains and organizes volunteer responders
requires: never speak for QSAR members

claims.spoken: Quinhagak is a Yup'ik village in western Alaska, off the road system.
claims.on_screen: QUINHAGAK · YUP'IK VILLAGE · NO ROADS IN
claims.verbatim_source: "one of 56 Yup’ik villages off the road system in western Alaska
requires: describe it with these facts only, never speak for residents

claims.spoken: It sits on the Bering Sea coast in the Yukon Kuskokwim Delta.
claims.verbatim_source: "Quinhagak, Alaska, lies along the Bering Sea coast in the Yukon–Kuskokwim Delta

claims.spoken: The local team already uses small drones with regular and infrared cameras.
claims.verbatim_source: "QSAR operators also use small quadrotor UASs equipped with EO/IR sensors

claims.spoken: The flights took place on July 17th and 18th under overcast skies.
claims.verbatim_source: "Flights were conducted on July 17–18, 2026, under overcast conditions
requires: summer season on screen, green tundra, no snow

claims.spoken: They flew over a mudflat on the Bering Sea coast and a patch of swamp grass near the Arolik River.
claims.verbatim_source: "a patch of swamp grass near the Arolik river
requires: companion excerpt reads "a mudflat on the coast of the Bering sea"
only two scenes were tested

claims.spoken: It was a simulation. The researchers laid out items to stage a search scenario.
claims.on_screen: A STAGED SEARCH · NOT A REAL RESCUE
claims.verbatim_source: "To simulate a QSAR mission scenario, we arranged relevant items.
requires: objects laid out by researchers, never a real search
no claim that anyone was found

claims.spoken: The items included waders, jackets, boots, nets, life jackets, buckets and buoys.
claims.verbatim_source: "fishing and marine equipment (nets, life jackets, buckets, buoys)
requires: companion excerpts read "clothing (waders, jackets, boots)" and "outdoor recreation gear (tarps, backpacks, storage canisters)"

claims.spoken: Most of the items were donated by the community.
claims.on_screen: ITEMS MOSTLY DONATED BY THE COMMUNITY
claims.verbatim_source: "mostly donated by the community
requires: say mostly
researchers arranged the items
no motive or sentiment for the community

claims.spoken: On the mudflat, about 56% of the system's flags were real objects, and it found 55% of them.
claims.verbatim_source: "SABL detects 55.08% of annotated objects in Mudflat and 29.20% in Swamp Grass
requires: mudflat precision 56.01 in Table II, the abstract gives approximately 56% and 99%
a preprint, not peer reviewed

claims.spoken: In the swamp grass, about 99% of flags were real objects, but it found only 29% of them.
claims.verbatim_source: "SABL detects 55.08% of annotated objects in Mudflat and 29.20% in Swamp Grass
requires: swamp grass precision 98.64 in Table II, the abstract says approximately 99%
each scene's figures come from its own threshold

claims.spoken: The authors say recall is still limited.
claims.verbatim_source: "First, object-level recall remains limited: at the reported operating points, SABL detects 55.08% of annotated objects
requires: the authors' own admission

claims.spoken: Part of the reason is that the filtering that cuts false alarms can also throw away real detections.
claims.verbatim_source: "Spatial filtering can suppress true detections alongside false-positives
requires: companion excerpt reads "higher τ can suppress detections of camouflaged objects"

claims.spoken: Testing covered just two scenes, both in subarctic tundra.
claims.verbatim_source: "Second, our evaluation is limited to two scenes in the subarctic tundra

claims.spoken: The authors say SABL should help existing search methods, not replace them.
claims.verbatim_source: "should, for this reason, be viewed as a tool for augmenting existing WSAR methods through identifying candidate search
requires: the paper's framing

claims.spoken: They also want to build it into real search workflows with people in the loop.
claims.verbatim_source: "integrating SABL into real human-in-the-loop WSAR workflows
requires: not used in a real search yet
